sources.title: ATO: Tax invoices, including eInvoicing and recipient-created tax invoices
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 18 September 2026): tax invoice requirements by sale value, eInvoices issued under the A-NZ Peppol specification treated as intended to be tax invoices, and the conditions and issuer checks for recipient-created tax invoices. Thresholds and time limits are read from the page at use time, not from this record.

sources.title: ASD: Learn about account compromise (How to prevent business email compromise)
sources.fact: Read 26 September 2026 at the retired address; reviewed by Ryan Duguid at this address on 20 October 2026. Recommends an approval process for requests to change payment details or make a large transfer, and verifying such a request by calling the sender on a known and verified phone number, not one given in the email. No legal rule, rate or threshold is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Guidance for small and medium businesses, not law. The firm's own payment approval policy governs. The automated refresh could not retrieve the page on 26 September 2026 (connection closed); it opened normally in a browser. Repointed on 20 October 2026: the original preventing-business-email-compromise page now returns 404, and the same two recommendations appear under 'How to prevent business email compromise' on this page.

sources.title: Peppol Authority: PINT A-NZ Billing release notes
sources.fact: Primary-source discovery only; no human-reviewed current-law fact is recorded.
sources.limitations: Indexed by an agent on 26 October 2026 because the ATO tax invoice page names the A-NZ Peppol specification without a version. Until a person accepts the pending baseline, the weekly sweep reports this record as baseline-required; after acceptance, later sweeps report a change to the release notes. Specification release notes, not law: the ATO page governs which eInvoices are treated as tax invoices. Human source approval remains pending. Read the current release and its jurisdiction rules at use time.
